paper_title: Deep learning to estimate lung disease mortality from chest radiographs
prediction_task: Lung disease mortality risk prediction from routine chest X-rays (CXR Lung-Risk)

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: DL model description is vague: loss function completely missing, training details (optimizer, dev split, epochs) absent, image preprocessing completely missing (DICOM→PNG, dimensions, cropping, augmentation). Why 20 models with random hyperparameters? How are they combined? Extreme ensemble learning is only used in ML contests but rarely in clinical settings.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added complete training pipeline details, preprocessing steps, and individual model performance.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: How does each individual model perform? Using 20-model ensemble is unacceptable without showing individual performance. This is extreme ensemble that would not be practical clinically.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added individual model performance table showing ensemble is necessary for stability.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: In supplemental Fig 3B, lung-risk HR of [65,75] category is not significant in multivariate model. The claim 'CXR Lung-Risk remained independently associated with lung disease mortality in both subpopulations' is misleading.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Corrected the claim with appropriate caveats.

reviewer_strengths.text: Novel problem for deep learning — finding risk of lung disease mortality from regular radiographs. Evidence suggests DL can identify elevated risk subjects.
